resources.string: Help
AstroClock measures time by astronomical standards.\nCycles\nTime is measured according to three natural cycles:

string.name: daycycle
string.li: Day \tOne rotation every 24 hours. \tHand at 12 o\'clock position at mid-day.

string.name: mooncycle
string.li: Moon\tOne rotation every 29.53 days.\tHand at 12 o\'clock position at full moon.

string.name: yearcycle
string.li: Year\tOne rotation every 365.25 days.\tHand at 12 o\'clock postion at the longest day of the year.

resources.string: The hands always turn in clockwise direction but the 12 o\'clock positions could be different in some themes.
Sun rise & Sun set\nWithin the day cylce are indicators showing the start and end of day and night.
Status Bar Notifications\nBy enabling alerts you will receive recurring notifications on selected events.
Homescreen\nAstroClock also comes with a homescreen widget and a low power live wallpaper.
Make your own Theme\nFor instructions on creating your own theme and sharing it with others, please visit android.arnodenhond.com/apps/astroclock/skins
Receive Broadcasts\nAstroClock sends out broadcast intents which your apps can receive. See android.arnodenhond.com/apps/astroclock/broadcast-intents for more information
Disclaimer\nThis app does not contain spyware or otherwise misbehave in any way. Some screens are known to burn in afterimages when displaying the same graphics over a long period.

About me\nThis app has been under semi-continuous development on evenings and weekends since April 2009 by Arno den Hond from Amsterdam (The Netherlands) on a MacBook Pro and has been tested on a Motorola Droid, a Samsung Galaxy Tab, an Asus Transformer and a LG Optimus 3D

Credits\nMany thanks to the graphics artists whose names are listed in the themes screen. Kostas of kanguro.fi inspired me on writing a user-friendly promo text. This app would not have been possible without the outstanding effort of engineers at google.com who made Android.
